accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS ELA SL.4.1 and SL.5.1: 'come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic' (SL.4.1a), 'pose and respond to specific questions' (SL.4.1c) and 'review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion' (SL.4.1d). The KS2 spoken language statements quoted in the adult text (justify answers and opinions; consider and evaluate different viewpoints) match the 2013 English programme of study. The fact sheet is labelled as a made-up class text and every fact quoted in replies and items (40 kg, 1 hour on Friday, watering 3 times a week, 25 pupils) matches the sheet exactly.

misconceptions.evidence: Each scene targets a documented weakness in primary discussion work: preparing by copying the text (pack scene card and challenge 'copy'), contributing with no reason (The garden is good, No it isn't!, challenge 'noreason'), vague references such as 'I read something once' (cite scene and 'vague'), closed yes/no questions that end the talk (ask scene, 'closed') and the belief that changing your mind is losing (prediction in step 5, 'stuck').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagprepdisc is built on one fact sheet that stays on screen: evidence cards and replies light up the exact line of the sheet they cite, and the pack scene checks off fact, question and view-with-reason chips in the notes bag. That preparation-to-talk link is the topic's own mechanism; flagbuildon (building on others' ideas) has no source text or notes. The gate measured the source under 30% similar to every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Wrong cards are refused with the reason (copying is not preparing; everyone says so is not evidence; probably is a guess), so the learner works out what counts as preparation before the step text confirms it. Replying to Mia, Leo and Ana is only possible with a card that names a fact, and the sheet highlight shows why that matters: others can check it. The final scene builds the full 'At first I thought..., but then Ana pointed out..., now I think..., because...' sentence and reads it back.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 offers 'Copy out the whole text', which many 8 to 10 year olds believe is thorough preparation; the pack scene then refuses that card. Step 2 offers 'Everyone says so', which the scene refuses as not evidence. Step 5 offers 'No, stick to your first view', which the sentence-building scene shows is weaker than explaining a change caused by evidence.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six why() messages name the exact slip: copying everything (copy), having no notes at all (none), giving no reason or evidence (noreason), a vague reference others cannot check (vague), a closed yes/no question (closed), and hiding or denying a change of mind (stuck). Every wrong option in QS maps to one of them.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (notes, fact, question, view, because, check), with the curriculum terms open question and closed question explained in place. Canvas cards are under 12 words. learn/validate_lessons.py readability passed for learner kid text and the adult text stays within the 9.5 limit.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs carry one step each: get ready with short notes, the three parts of a note, point to the text, then open questions and explaining a change of mind. Adult paragraphs give standards, how to coach it at home, named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark after each Show me and mid-demo: the fact sheet uses one font size for all four lines and the cited line turns bold on a yellow band; the three point boxes in step 2 wrap their labels above the placed evidence; pool cards are about 150 px wide in two columns; the sentence stack in step 5 keeps each start on the left and the dropped part on the right without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button route: Pick a card, then a button for each box, plus Cancel. Each action updates the canvas aria-label and the live region, including refusal reasons and the full sentence in step 5. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations; canvas text is dark ink on white, pale yellow or pale green cards in both themes.
